topic: The 12 Schedules of the Indian Constitution
description: The original Indian Constitution adopted in 1950 consisted of only 8 Schedules. Over time, 4 more schedules were added through various Constitutional Amendment Acts (CAAs), bringing the total number of schedules to 12 today.

sections.title: Initial Schedules: 1 to 4
sections.description: The first four schedules dealing with territories, emoluments, oaths, and representation in the upper house.

polity_articles.provision: Names of the States and Union Territories (UTs) and their territorial jurisdiction.
polity_articles.details: Corresponds to Articles 1 and 4. Currently, India has 28 States and 8 UTs.

polity_articles.provision: Provisions relating to the salaries, emoluments, allowances, and privileges of constitutional dignitaries.
polity_articles.details: Includes the President, Governors, Judges of SC/HC, and CAG. Note: The Prime Minister and Chief Ministers are NOT mentioned in this schedule.

polity_articles.provision: Forms of Oaths or Affirmations for various candidates and constitutional functionaries.
polity_articles.details: Note: The oaths of the President, Vice-President, and Governor are NOT in this schedule; they are provided in their respective Articles (60, 69, and 159).

polity_articles.provision: Allocation of seats in the Rajya Sabha (Council of States) to the States and Union Territories.
polity_articles.details: Seats are allocated on the basis of the population of the respective states.

sections.title: Administration of Tribal Areas: Schedules 5 and 6
sections.description: Schedules dealing exclusively with the administration of scheduled and tribal areas to protect indigenous rights.

polity_articles.provision: Provisions relating to the administration and control of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes.
polity_articles.details: Applies to all states in India EXCEPT the four North-Eastern states mentioned in the Sixth Schedule. Corresponds to Article 244(1).

polity_articles.provision: Provisions relating to the administration of Tribal Areas in the states of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram.
polity_articles.details: Can be memorized using the acronym 'AMTM'. It provides for the creation of Autonomous District Councils (ADCs). Corresponds to Articles 244(2) and 275(1).

sections.title: Federalism and Languages: Schedules 7 and 8
sections.description: Schedules establishing the division of legislative powers and the officially recognized languages of the Republic.

polity_articles.provision: Division of powers between the Union and the States in terms of three lists: Union List, State List, and Concurrent List.
polity_articles.details: Corresponds to Article 246. Originally, the Union List had 97 subjects (now 100), State List had 66 (now 61), and Concurrent List had 47 (now 52).

polity_articles.provision: Languages officially recognized by the Constitution.
polity_articles.details: Originally contained 14 languages; currently has 22. Sindhi (21st CAA), Konkani, Manipuri, Nepali (71st CAA), and Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, Santhali (92nd CAA) were added later.

sections.title: Schedules Added via Amendments: 9 to 12
sections.description: The four schedules added to the Constitution post-1950 to address land reforms, political defection, and local self-government.

polity_articles.provision: Acts and regulations of the state legislatures dealing with land reforms and abolition of the Zamindari system.
polity_articles.details: Added by the 1st Constitutional Amendment Act (1951) to protect these laws from judicial review on the grounds of violation of Fundamental Rights.

polity_articles.provision: Provisions relating to the disqualification of the members of Parliament and State Legislatures on the ground of defection.
polity_articles.details: Popularly known as the 'Anti-Defection Law'. Added by the 52nd Constitutional Amendment Act (1985).

polity_articles.provision: Specifies the powers, authority, and responsibilities of Panchayats (Rural Local Government).
polity_articles.details: Added by the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act (1992). It contains 29 functional items.

polity_articles.provision: Specifies the powers, authority, and responsibilities of Municipalities (Urban Local Government).
polity_articles.details: Added by the 74th Constitutional Amendment Act (1992). It contains 18 functional items.

sections.title: Memory Trick and Important Facts
sections.description: The most widely used mnemonic to remember the 12 schedules sequentially and crucial exam-oriented facts.

key_associations.extra_info: Names and extents of States and UTs
Seat allocation in the Upper House

important_facts.fact: The mnemonic 'TEARS OF OLD PM' helps memorize the 12 schedules in their exact order.

In the landmark 'I.R. Coelho case' (2007), the Supreme Court ruled that laws placed in the 9th Schedule on or after April 24, 1973 (the date of the Kesavananda Bharati verdict) are open to judicial review and are not absolutely immune.
